content: 1. Increase the dose of didanosine to 250 mg/day if the patient weighs more than 60 kg, and decrease it to 200 mg/day if the patient weighs less than 60 kg. 2. Didanosine reduces the absorption and effectiveness of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both drugs. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Oral tetracycline should not be administered simultaneously with didanosine (chewable tablets or oral solution). Alternative treatments should be considered if available. Tetracycline antibiotics should be taken 1 hour before or 4 hours after didanosine administration. 3. Co-administration of didanosine and tinidazole may increase the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is an enhanced risk of peripheral neuropathy. 4. Both tipranavir and didanosine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Additionally, tipranavir decreases the levels of didanosine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 5. Ublituximab reduces the effects of didanosine through immunosuppressive mechanisms, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 6. Co-administration of valganciclovir and didanosine increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and alternatives should be considered if available. There is an increased risk of hematologic toxicity. 7. Didanosine and valoctocogene roxaparvovec both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Medications that may cause hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec can further elevate liver enzyme levels. These medications should be closely monitored, and alternative treatments should be considered in cases of potential drug interactions. 8. Didanosine and vincristine (or vincristine liposomal) may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is an enhanced risk of peripheral neuropathy. 9. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Co-administration of didanosine and ethanol may increase the toxicity of both substances due to pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown, but there is an enhanced risk of pancreatitis. 11. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of ferric carboxymaltose, ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution should be administered 2 hours before or several hours after these iron supplements. 12. Food decreases the levels of didanosine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of didanosine. The clinical significance is unknown. 13. Didanosine and isoniazid may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown, but there is an enhanced risk of peripheral neuropathy. 14. Didanosine and metronidazole may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown, but there is an enhanced risk of peripheral neuropathy. 15. Didanosine increases the levels of nelfinavir by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 16. Didanosine and nitrofurantoin may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown, but there is an enhanced risk of peripheral neuropathy. 17. Didanosine and pentamidine may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown, but there is an enhanced risk of pancreatitis. 18. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. Didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution should be administered 2 hours before or several hours after polysaccharide iron. 19. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. Didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution should be administered 2 hours before or several hours after posaconazole. 20. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Valganciclovir increases the levels of didanosine by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Zidovudine increases the levels of didanosine by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Both abacavir and didanosine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Allopurinol increases the levels of didanosine through an unknown mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Both atazanavir and didanosine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Didanosine and atidarsagene autotemcel should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Patients should avoid antiretroviral therapy for at least 1 month before cell mobilization or until the expected duration for medication elimination. 27. Didanosine and betibeglogene autotemcel should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. Patients should avoid antiretroviral therapy for at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 28. Didanosine and busulfan may increase each other’s toxicity. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Pretomanid regimens associated with hepatotoxicity should avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 29. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. Didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution should be administered 2 hours before or several hours after carbonyl iron. 30. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of cefpodoxime and cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. Didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution should be administered 2 hours before or several hours after these antibiotics. 31. Didanosine decreases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Oral ciprofloxacin should not be administered simultaneously with didanosine (chewable tablets or oral solution). Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after didanosine. 32. Didanosine and cisplatin may increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is an enhanced risk of peripheral neuropathy. 33. Didanosine increases the toxicity of dapsone through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as there may be an increased risk of nerve damage. 34. Darunavir reduces the levels or effects of didanosine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Didanosine should be administered 1 hour before or 2 hours after darunavir/ritonavir. Monitor closely. 35. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Didanosine reduces the levels or effects of demeclocycline and doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution should be administered 2 hours before or several hours after these antibiotics. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 37. Didanosine and efavirenz may enhance each other’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is an increased risk of liver toxicity. 38. Didanosine and elivaldogene autotemcel should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with stem cell mobilization and apheresis. Patients should avoid antiretroviral therapy for at least 1 month before initiating stem cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 39. Didanosine and elvitegravir should be administered with caution. Didanosine must be taken on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after elvitegravir (which is taken with food). 40. Didanosine and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF should not be co-administered. This combination is contraindicated, as elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be combined with other antiretrovirals. 41. Febuxostat increases the levels of didanosine by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 42. Ganciclovir increases the levels of didanosine by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely.
